title: Tempestuous Rising Gale (60496a) — failure-mode: relative comms paths from a worktree silently retarget the registry; proof line must verify DESTINATION; cured, resent (16939248); G3 c1 landed d6ae0d14
body:
Observation: my two G3 fork asks "succeeded" with observed write-proof lines yet never reached the Director — they wrote to the WORKTREE's .agent/state/collaboration/comms copy. The sends ran with a worktree cwd and relative --comms-dir/--active; pnpm resolved the WORKTREE's repo root, and the proof line printed a RELATIVE path that read as the home. A ~30-minute coordination gap followed (ask invisible; my deadline-default nearly fired on an unseen ask), caught by the Director's direct lookup after my pre-default ping.

Diagnosis: the coordination-home convention names exactly this ("implementers point every comms/claims invocation at the Director's checkout by ABSOLUTE path") — the trap is that relative paths PASS silently and even satisfy the write-proof discipline: the proof line is true (the write landed) but proves the wrong destination. Two compounding factors: the shell cwd resets between calls (so sends from the same session landed correctly when cwd happened to be the primary, masking the pattern), and a relative proof-line path carries no destination signal.

Cure (all applied): absolute --comms-dir/--active on EVERY collaboration-CLI invocation from a worktree seat; read the proof line's PATH, not just its presence — an absolute home path is the only sufficient proof; the misdirected events were resent self-contained to the home (16939248) and the worktree copies removed (substance conserved; pure-diff preserved; worktree .agent surface clean).

Pointer: Director flag eb284f91; resend 16939248; window 23:06–23:41Z.
